lead: No natural product has grade A evidence in rheumatoid arthritis; several were tested as additions to disease-modifying medicines; none is shown to replace them. For fish oil (omega-3), a 2024 meta-analysis of 18 randomized trials found fewer tender joints, while another of 23 placebo-controlled trials found only small, uncertain effects (grade B). Curcumin, vitamin D and probiotics also have meta-analyses with mixed or very-low-certainty results (grade B), and thunder god vine has randomized trials alongside reports of intestinal, reproductive, liver and kidney toxicity from an evidence synthesis that was not limited to rheumatoid arthritis; a 2023 meta-analysis found no increase in most adverse events when the extract was added to methotrexate.

grade_key.A: Meta-analysis, or at least 2 randomized trials with low risk of bias and a consistent benefit
grade_key.B: 1 good randomized trial, or several randomized trials with mixed results
grade_key.C: Observational studies, small pilots or open-label trials only
grade_key.Negative: Randomized trials found no benefit over placebo

disclaimer: This page summarizes published research. It is not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before starting any supplement, especially if you take other medicines.

products.name: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10)
products.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 54 people with active disease took CoQ10 100 mg a day or placebo for 2 months; the disease activity score (DAS-28), pain score and tender and swollen joint counts were better in the CoQ10 group after the trial. A second double-blind randomized trial in 44 people, with the same amount and duration, measured blood markers only: an oxidative stress marker fell, and there was no difference in interleukin-6. The abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.

products.name: Curcumin (turmeric extract)
products.summary: A 2025 meta-analysis of 6 placebo-controlled randomized trials with 244 people found better disease activity scores (DAS28), joint counts, pain scores and inflammatory markers with curcumin, but rated the certainty of nearly every outcome very low and called for larger trials. A second 2025 meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials also found lower DAS28, ESR and CRP, with substantial differences between trials. In a randomized pilot trial, 45 people received curcumin 500 mg alone, the anti-inflammatory drug diclofenac alone, or both; DAS scores changed significantly in all three groups. A 2020 systematic review concluded that no conclusion could be drawn because the curcumin studies were of low quality. The meta-analysis abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: In the 45-person pilot trial, the authors reported that curcumin was not related to any adverse events. The 2025 meta-analysis called for further trials to verify safety. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Turmeric and curcumin
general_safety.short: Case series link turmeric supplements to liver injury, sometimes severe. Curcumin may alter levels of some drugs, including anticoagulants, mostly in non-clinical studies.

products.name: Gamma-linolenic acid (evening primrose, borage or blackcurrant seed oil)
products.summary: A 2011 Cochrane review pooled 7 studies of oils containing gamma-linolenic acid and found lower pain intensity and less disability than with placebo; the reviewers called this moderate evidence of some benefit in relieving symptoms. In a separate randomized trial, 56 people with active disease took 2.8 g a day of gamma-linolenic acid or placebo for 6 months, and 14 of 22 on the acid had a meaningful response against 4 of 19 on placebo; the authors noted that it is usually taken in far lower amounts than the trial used. These abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: In the Cochrane review, adverse events were reported by 20% of people taking gamma-linolenic acid and 3% taking placebo, a difference that was not statistically significant. The 56-person trial described it as well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Gamma-linolenic acid
general_safety.short: In eczema trials, evening primrose and borage oil had the same mild, mainly gastrointestinal effects as placebo. One study found evening primrose oil may increase bleeding in people on warfarin.

products.name: Garlic
products.summary: Two reports of randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials each describe 70 women given garlic 1,000 mg a day or placebo for 8 weeks. In one, pain intensity, tender joint count, disease activity score (DAS-28) and fatigue fell more with garlic than with placebo, as did CRP, while ESR did not change. In the other, pain after activity and disability scores decreased compared with placebo. The abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Garlic
general_safety.short: Case reports of altered platelet function and clotting, with possible bleeding risk, and of burns from raw garlic on skin. May enhance warfarin; lowered saquinavir levels in a study.

products.name: Ginger
products.summary: In a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 people with active disease took ginger powder 1500 mg a day or placebo; the fall in disease activity score was significant within the ginger group and between the two groups. A second report, in 66 people given 1.5 g a day or placebo, found a decline in CRP. A 2020 systematic review said the risk of bias of the spice studies is difficult to assess and the data are too limited to recommend them in daily practice. The abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Ginger
general_safety.short: Pregnancy trials found no significant rise in miscarriage (with wide uncertainty), heartburn or drowsiness. A warfarin review flags possible added bleeding risk.

products.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
products.summary: Results are mixed. A 2024 meta-analysis of 4 randomized trials with 204 people concluded that NAC used as an add-on lowered disease activity and ESR, with no effect on oxidative stress. Two separate trials point the other way on disease activity: in a 3-month placebo-controlled trial in 74 people (600 mg twice a day), NAC did not improve the disease activity score, ESR or CRP compared with placebo; and in a 12-week trial in 51 people on standard treatment, the disease activity score and ESR did not differ between groups, though pain, global health and disability scores improved more with NAC. The authors of the 74-person trial stated that NAC should not be used as a replacement for routine rheumatoid arthritis medicines.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
general_safety.short: In a review of 41 reports in chronic lung disease, stomach and bowel symptoms occurred but were no more common than in control groups, including at higher doses.

products.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
products.summary: A 2024 meta-analysis of 18 randomized trials with 1018 people found fewer tender joints with omega-3 supplements, while changes in the disease activity score (DAS28) and the inflammatory markers ESR and CRP were not statistically significant. Another 2024 meta-analysis, of 23 placebo-controlled trials, found only small effects on pain and on tender and swollen joint counts, with confidence intervals that included no effect; it rated the certainty mostly very low or low and concluded the clinical benefit might be limited. A 2012 meta-analysis of 10 trials found lower use of anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) at more than 2.7 g a day for more than 3 months, but joint counts did not improve significantly, and the 23-trial review suggested the painkiller finding may have been biased by inadequate blinding. These abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
general_safety.short: Linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation in cardiovascular trials, more so above 1 g/day; diarrhoea and altered taste were more likely than with placebo; bleeding findings are mixed.

products.name: Probiotics
products.summary: Results are mixed. A 2022 meta-analysis covering 8 trials in 344 people with rheumatoid arthritis found lower CRP with probiotics, but no difference from placebo in the disease activity score (DAS28) once trials at high risk of bias were excluded; the authors said the evidence does not allow probiotics to be proposed for disease control. A 2017 meta-analysis of 9 trials in 361 people also found no difference in disease activity score. A 2023 meta-analysis of 12 trials of gut-microbe supplements used as add-on therapy found a lower disease activity score but no significant effect on pain or ESR. In one randomized double-blind trial in women on stable medication, 46 of whom were analysed, 8 weeks of Lactobacillus casei lowered CRP, tender and swollen joint counts and DAS28.
products.safety_interactions: In the Lactobacillus casei trial, no adverse effects were reported for the supplement. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Probiotics
general_safety.short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.

products.name: Purslane
products.summary: In a 12-week double-blinded randomized trial, 86 people took a 500 mg purslane capsule twice a day or placebo, and 77 completed the study. The abstract reports that pain scores, tender and swollen joint counts and the disease activity score (DAS28) fell in the purslane group, without stating a comparison with placebo for these; only morning stiffness and the physician's global assessment are stated as lower than in the placebo group at the end of the trial. The abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Purslane
general_safety.short: Case report: acute kidney injury from oxalate in two elderly patients after eating large amounts. In two trials adverse events were mild to moderate and did not differ significantly from placebo.

citations.label: Karimi et al., 2024, Phytomedicine
citations.title: The effect of purslane supplementation on clinical outcomes, inflammatory and antioxidant markers in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A parallel double-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial.

products.name: Rose hip
products.summary: In a 6-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 89 people, rose hip powder 5 g a day was compared with placebo. Disability scores (the trial's main outcome) improved slightly with rose hip and worsened slightly with placebo, a significant difference. Pain scores and use of pain medicines did not differ between groups, and the difference in disease activity score (DAS-28) did not reach statistical significance (p=0.056). The authors describe rose hip as an additional treatment.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Rose hip
general_safety.short: A mechanism-focused review states that trials showed excellent tolerability; a meta-analysis of three manufacturer-supported trials said safety still needs a large, long-term trial.

citations.label: Willich et al., 2010, Phytomedicine
citations.title: Rose hip herbal remedy in patients with rheumatoid arthritis - a randomised controlled trial.

products.name: Saffron
products.summary: In a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 66 women with active disease took saffron 100 mg a day or placebo. Tender and swollen joint counts, pain scores and the disease activity score (DAS28) improved with saffron compared with placebo; differences in inflammatory and oxidative blood markers were not significant between groups. The trial abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs. A 2021 systematic review of saffron added to standard treatment in rheumatic diseases found the evidence not enough to establish a direction of effect.
products.safety_interactions: In the 66-person trial, no adverse effects were reported by the patients. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Saffron
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 12 depression studies, adverse effects were no more common than with placebo. In a 1-week volunteer study the higher dose lowered standing blood pressure.

products.name: Selenium
products.summary: Results are mixed. A 2025 meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials with 367 people found lower pain scores and a lower joint tenderness index with selenium, but no significant effect on ESR, CRP, morning stiffness or joint swelling. Two separate trials found no difference from placebo: a double-blind trial in 55 people given selenium-enriched yeast for 90 days concluded there was no clinical benefit, and a 12-week double-blind trial in 59 people found no between-group difference in disease activity scores. The abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Selenium
general_safety.short: Excess causes selenosis: diarrhoea, fatigue, hair loss, nail changes (outbreak from a mislabelled supplement). One trial found more type 2 diabetes; a pooled analysis was not significant.

products.name: Thunder god vine (Tripterygium wilfordii)
products.summary: Extracts of thunder god vine have been tested both alone and with methotrexate. A 2023 meta-analysis of 14 randomized trials with 1446 people found higher response and remission rates when the extract was added to methotrexate than with methotrexate alone; the authors said higher-quality double-blind trials could change these conclusions. In an open-label randomized trial in 207 people, 55.1% reached a 50% improvement response with the extract alone, 46.4% with methotrexate alone and 76.8% with both; people in the single-drug groups whose disease activity score had fallen by less than 30% at week 12 were switched to the combination. In a randomized trial in 121 people who had stopped disease-modifying drugs, more people responded to the extract than to sulfasalazine, but outcome data were available for only 62 people at 24 weeks. A Cochrane review said these products may reduce some symptoms but that oral use may be associated with several side effects.
products.safety_interactions: Toxicity is the main concern, although the findings are not all in one direction. A 2019 evidence synthesis of 46 studies of a tripterygium glycoside preparation, in 2437 people (the abstract names no condition, so this is not limited to rheumatoid arthritis), estimated that 30.75% had adverse events and 4.68% had severe ones; the severe-event estimate is imprecise (95% confidence interval 0 to 12.7%). It found intestinal, reproductive, liver, kidney, blood and skin toxicity. In the 121-person randomized trial, the frequency of adverse events was similar with the extract and with sulfasalazine. The 2023 meta-analysis found that adding the extract to methotrexate did not increase the risk of most adverse events and reduced the risk of infection and liver adverse events. In the 207-person trial, irregular menstruation developed in 7 women taking the extract alone, 3 taking methotrexate alone and 5 taking both; the difference between the extract and methotrexate was not statistically significant. The Cochrane review noted that one study reported serious side effects with oral use, and that in the follow-up studies all side effects were mild to moderate and resolved after the treatment stopped. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Thunder god vine (Tripterygium wilfordii)
general_safety.short: Pooled clinical studies: about 31% of users had adverse events, affecting gut, reproductive system, liver, kidney, blood and skin. Reviews describe reduced fertility and loss of periods.

products.name: Total glucosides of paeony
products.summary: Total glucosides of paeony has been tested mainly as an addition to disease-modifying drugs. A 2018 meta-analysis of 8 randomized trials with 522 people found that adding it to methotrexate gave better overall response, lower ESR and fewer swollen joints than methotrexate alone, with no significant difference in CRP, morning stiffness or tender joint count; the authors rated the included trials as methodologically poor. A 2023 meta-analysis found it may improve the disease activity score (DAS28) and lower ESR and CRP, but called the trials low quality. A 2025 umbrella review rated the evidence for its effects on disease activity score and ESR as low quality.
products.safety_interactions: A 2021 meta-analysis of 39 studies (randomized trials and cohort studies) with 3680 people found fewer liver adverse effects and less leukopenia (low white cell count) when paeony glucosides were added to conventional treatment, mostly disease-modifying drugs, than with that treatment alone. In the subgroups, the liver finding was statistically significant only where the treatment included leflunomide (leflunomide alone, or methotrexate plus leflunomide), and for leukopenia the abstract reports a significant subgroup difference for methotrexate plus leflunomide. The 2023 meta-analysis, which covered five types of inflammatory arthritis, reported that adding it did not increase adverse events; the abstract does not give this finding separately for rheumatoid arthritis. Other interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Total glucosides of paeony
general_safety.short: Trials report diarrhoea or stomach discomfort as the commonest side effects, with no severe events; added to standard drugs it did not raise adverse reactions.

products.name: Type II collagen (oral)
products.summary: Results are mixed and mostly null. A 1993 randomized double-blind trial in 60 people with severe disease found fewer swollen and tender joints after 3 months of chicken type II collagen but not with placebo. A 24-week trial in 274 people testing four amounts found a significant difference from placebo only at the lowest amount and on only one of three sets of response criteria. Three other placebo-controlled trials found no significant benefit: one in 190 people who added bovine collagen to their existing medicines for 6 months, in which several clinical variables differed significantly and all of those favoured placebo, one in 60 people over 6 months, and one in 90 people with early disease over 12 weeks. In a 24-week double-blind trial in 503 people comparing chicken collagen with methotrexate, response rates were lower with collagen. Apart from the 190-person add-on trial, the abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: Two trials reported no side effects or no adverse events related to collagen, and the methotrexate comparison found fewer and milder side effects with collagen. In the early-disease trial, 2 people withdrew because of nausea. The authors of one 6-month trial raised the possibility that oral collagen may induce disease flares in a subgroup of patients. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Collagen
general_safety.short: In osteoarthritis trials the most reported adverse events were mild to moderate gastrointestinal complaints; a review of 11 skin trials reported no adverse events.

products.name: Vitamin D
products.summary: Results are mixed. The abstract of a 2024 meta-analysis of 11 randomized trials with 3049 people is internally inconsistent: its conclusion states that vitamin D supplements did not significantly reduce CRP, ESR, the disease activity score (DAS28) or disability scores, and that responses varied widely between trials, yet the same abstract reports a pooled analysis in which pain scores and two versions of the disease activity score (DAS28-CRP and DAS28-ESR) were significantly lower. A 2020 meta-analysis of 6 trials with 438 people found small improvements in DAS28, ESR and tender joint count compared with placebo, but not in other outcomes. These abstracts do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Vitamin D
general_safety.short: Long-term supplementation raised the risk of high blood calcium and high urine calcium in trials, but not kidney stones; toxicity from extremely high doses is rare but serious.

products.name: Vitamin E
products.summary: In a 12-week randomized double-blind trial, 42 people already taking anti-rheumatic drugs added vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol 600 mg twice a day) or placebo. Pain measures fell with vitamin E compared with placebo, but clinical signs of inflammation and laboratory inflammatory markers did not change. A 2023 meta-analysis of 9 publications, whose control groups received placebo, other drugs or external therapy, reported pooled differences in tender and swollen joints whose confidence intervals included no difference.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Vitamin E
general_safety.short: Meta-analyses link vitamin E to more haemorrhagic strokes and, at high doses, higher mortality; in the SELECT trial it raised prostate cancer risk in healthy men.

products.name: Black seed oil (Nigella sativa)
products.summary: In a 2-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 43 women with mild to moderate disease, one gram a day of black seed oil lowered CRP, the disease activity score (DAS-28) and the number of swollen joints compared with baseline and with placebo. A second randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 42 people, lasting 8 weeks, measured blood markers only, with mixed results. In another study, 40 women on disease-modifying drugs all took placebo capsules for a month and then black seed oil for a month; DAS-28 was lower after the oil. The abstracts of the two randomized trials do not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs. A 2020 systematic review concluded that the limited clinical studies did not show a change in inflammatory and oxidative markers. Graded C because the only randomized trial reporting clinical outcomes had 43 women; the other studies measured blood markers only or had no separate control group.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Black seed (Nigella sativa) oil
general_safety.short: Trials reported no serious adverse events. A laboratory study predicts its main compound, thymoquinone, could interact with warfarin; this has not been shown in patients.

products.name: Boron (calcium fructoborate or borax)
products.summary: In a 60-day double-blind randomized placebo-controlled pilot study, 80 people with active disease who were maintained on the biologic drug etanercept added calcium fructoborate, sodium tetraborate (each supplying 6 mg of boron a day) or placebo; 72 completed it. Both forms of boron improved clinical scores and lowered ESR and CRP compared with baseline and with placebo. Graded C as a single pilot study.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Boron
general_safety.short: Human safety has not been studied systematically; a review warns excessive use may be harmful. Boric acid poisoning has been fatal, and animal studies show reproductive toxicity.

citations.label: Hussain et al., 2017, J Intercult Ethnopharmacol
citations.title: The adjuvant use of calcium fructoborate and borax with etanercept in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: Pilot study.

products.name: Cinnamon
products.summary: In an 8-week randomized double-blind trial, 36 women took 4 capsules a day of 500 mg cinnamon powder or placebo. Compared with placebo, cinnamon lowered the disease activity score (DAS-28), pain scores, tender and swollen joint counts and CRP; ESR did not change. Graded C because the trial was small. The abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: In the 36-person trial, liver enzymes did not change significantly. Adverse events and interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited abstract.

general_safety.name: Cinnamon
general_safety.short: Most reported adverse events are gastrointestinal upset and allergic reactions. Its coumarin can harm the liver; one case report describes hepatitis when taken with a statin.

citations.label: Shishehbor et al., 2018, J Am Coll Nutr
citations.title: Cinnamon Consumption Improves Clinical Symptoms and Inflammatory Markers in Women With Rheumatoid Arthritis.

products.name: Hesperidin (as alpha-glucosyl hesperidin)
products.summary: In a 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 19 people who also received standard therapy, a drink containing 3 g of alpha-glucosyl hesperidin was taken every morning by 9 people and a placebo drink by 10. Three of 9 improved with hesperidin and 1 of 10 with placebo. Graded C because the trial was very small and the abstract reports no statistical comparison.
products.safety_interactions: The trial abstract reports that the product was given without any adverse effects. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

citations.label: Kometani et al., 2008, Immunopharmacol Immunotoxicol
citations.title: Effects of alpha-glucosylhesperidin, a bioactive food material, on collagen-induced arthritis in mice and rheumatoid arthritis in humans.

products.name: Quercetin
products.summary: In an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 50 women took quercetin 500 mg a day or placebo. Morning stiffness and pain fell with quercetin, and disease activity (DAS-28) and disability scores decreased compared with placebo. Tender and swollen joint counts did not differ between groups, and the change in ESR was not significant. Graded C because this is a single trial that was small and short. The abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Quercetin
general_safety.short: Human studies report rare, mild side effects; long-term high-dose safety is unknown. May alter levels of some drugs (CYP2C9, CYP2E1 and P-glycoprotein substrates).

citations.label: Javadi et al., 2017, J Am Coll Nutr
citations.title: The Effect of Quercetin on Inflammatory Factors and Clinical Symptoms in Women with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial.

products.name: Resveratrol
products.summary: In a randomized controlled trial without a placebo, 100 people were divided into two groups of 50: one took a resveratrol capsule of 1 g a day with their conventional treatment for 3 months, and the other had the regular treatment only. Swollen and tender joint counts, the 28-joint disease activity score, CRP and ESR were lower in the resveratrol group. Graded C because the comparison group received no placebo.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Resveratrol
general_safety.short: Generally well tolerated up to 1 g/day; 2.5 to 5 g/day caused mild to moderate gut symptoms. Changes CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP2C9 and CYP1A2 activity, so may interact with medicines.

citations.label: Khojah et al., 2018, Clin Rheumatol
citations.title: Resveratrol as an effective adjuvant therapy in the management of rheumatoid arthritis: a clinical study.

products.name: Sesamin (from sesame)
products.summary: In a 6-week randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 44 women took sesamin 200 mg a day or placebo. CRP and other inflammatory markers fell in the sesamin group compared with placebo, and the abstract reports fewer tender joints and less severe pain with sesamin, without stating whether that was a comparison with placebo. Graded C because the trial was small and short. The abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Sesamin
general_safety.short: No serious adverse events in a 28-day study of sesamin plus episesamin in 48 healthy people. Interaction evidence is laboratory and rat data only.

citations.label: Helli et al., 2019, Phytother Res
citations.title: A randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, evaluating the sesamin supplement effects on proteolytic enzymes, inflammatory markers, and clinical indices in women with rheumatoid arthritis.

products.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
products.summary: Two reports of randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, each describing 70 people given alpha-lipoic acid 1200 mg a day or placebo for 8 weeks, found no difference from placebo. One measured inflammatory markers (CRP, interleukin-6) and a marker of joint erosion; the other measured oxidative stress markers. Neither abstract reports joint counts, pain or a disease activity score, and neither says whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
general_safety.short: Trials: no more adverse events than placebo. Case reports link it to insulin autoimmune syndrome, a rare cause of low blood sugar, in genetically susceptible people.

citations.label: Mirtaheri et al., 2015, J Am Coll Nutr
citations.title: Effects of Alpha-Lipoic Acid Supplementation on Inflammatory Biomarkers and Matrix Metalloproteinase-3 in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients.

citations.label: Kolahi et al., 2019, Int J Vitam Nutr Res
citations.title: Oral administration of alpha-lipoic acid did not affect lipid peroxidation and antioxidant biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis patients.

products.name: Andrographis (king of bitters)
products.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 60 people with active disease took an Andrographis paniculata extract three times a day for 14 weeks. Joint pain intensity, the main outcome, did not differ significantly from placebo. Reductions in tender and swollen joints and in disability scores were reported as within-group changes in the extract group. The authors said a larger and longer trial is needed. The abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Andrographis
general_safety.short: Serious adverse events were very rare in trials; non-serious ones, mostly gut and skin complaints, were common. Spontaneous reports include allergic reactions such as anaphylaxis and angioedema.

citations.label: Burgos et al., 2009, Clin Rheumatol
citations.title: Efficacy of an Andrographis paniculata composition for the relief of rheumatoid arthritis symptoms: a prospective randomized placebo-controlled trial.

products.name: Melatonin
products.summary: In a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 64 people took melatonin 6 mg a day or placebo. The disease activity score (DAS-28) and ESR fell from baseline with melatonin (a within-group change), but neither differed from the placebo group. The authors concluded that melatonin had no beneficial effect on DAS-28 and should not replace routine rheumatoid arthritis drugs. The abstract does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Melatonin
general_safety.short: Trial adverse events were few and mostly mild (daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness); long-term data are limited. Drugs acting on CYP1A2 may slow its breakdown.

citations.label: Esalatmanesh et al., 2021, Clin Rheumatol
citations.title: Effects of melatonin supplementation on disease activity, oxidative stress, inflammatory, and metabolic parameters in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial.

products.name: Vitamin K1
products.summary: In an 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 64 women took vitamin K1 10 mg a day or placebo. A blood marker of joint destruction did not change, and rheumatoid factor did not differ between groups after adjustment. The abstract does not report joint counts or pain results, and does not say whether participants stayed on disease-modifying drugs.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Vitamin K
general_safety.short: Interacts with warfarin: changes in vitamin K intake alter anticoagulant control (INR). A review found multivitamins contain enough vitamin K1 to change coagulation measures.

citations.label: Shishavan et al., 2016, J Am Coll Nutr
citations.title: Effects of Vitamin K on Matrix Metalloproteinase-3 and Rheumatoid Factor in Women with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
